subject.title: Teams Meetings plugin documented as bundled but missing from stable npm build

question: Should `teams-meetings` be included in the next stable npm release, or should its public documentation state that the feature is unreleased until package acceptance proves it ships?
rationale: The source and public docs indicate an intended bundled plugin, but the supplied stable-install result conflicts with that expectation and only release owners can choose between immediate release inclusion and temporarily version-gated documentation.

options.title: Ship with package proof
options.body: Include the plugin in the next stable npm artifact and attach clean-install evidence that `plugins inspect`, setup, and bundled discovery work.

options.title: Version-gate documentation
options.body: Keep the feature off the stable-install path and change public docs to state its first supported release or installation path.

recommendation.title: Ship with package proof
recommendation.body: Include the plugin in the next stable npm artifact and attach clean-install evidence that `plugins inspect`, setup, and bundled discovery work.

likelyOwner.reason: Available repository history ties this person to adjacent documentation, making them the best low-confidence routing candidate for the docs-versus-release decision.
